Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Write True or False: (a) The edible part of coconut is the endocarp. (b) Apple has a fleshy thalamus.
questions.answer: (a) False – the edible part is the endosperm. (b) True.

questions.q: Match: (a) Bulliform cells (b) Guttation with (i) Xylem (ii) Hydathodes (iii) Monocot leaf (iv) Palisade parenchyma.
Fill in the blank: Conjoint, collateral and open vascular bundles are found in ______ stem.
questions.answer: dicot.

questions.q: Name the inflorescence: (a) Fig (b) Ocimum (tulsi).
questions.answer: (a) Hypanthodium. (b) Verticillaster.

questions.q: Name the type of fruit: (a) pea (b) wheat.
questions.answer: (a) Legume. (b) Caryopsis.

questions.q: Identify the stem modification: (a) potato (b) ginger.
questions.answer: (a) Tuber. (b) Rhizome.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Lateral branches of stem are exogenous in origin. (b) Monocot stems show secondary growth.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False.

questions.q: Match the placentation: (a) pea (b) china rose with (i) axile (ii) marginal.
Give the type of phyllotaxy: (a) mango (b) guava.
questions.answer: (a) Alternate. (b) Opposite superposed.

questions.q: Name the three parts of the pericarp of a mango and the edible part.
questions.answer: Epicarp, mesocarp and endocarp; the edible part is the mesocarp.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the term 'Hypanthodium' with an example.
questions.answer: An inflorescence with a hollow, cup-shaped receptacle with an apical opening (ostiole); male and female flowers lie on the inner wall; e.g. fig and peepal.

questions.q: What is a phylloclade? Give an example.
questions.answer: A green, flattened or cylindrical fleshy stem that photosynthesises and stores water; e.g. Opuntia (leaves are reduced to spines).

questions.q: Differentiate between a simple and a compound leaf (two points).
questions.answer: A simple leaf has an undivided lamina (or incisions not reaching the midrib); a compound leaf has leaflets, incisions reaching the midrib, and an axillary bud only at the base of the whole leaf.

questions.q: Write the difference between sapwood and heartwood (two points).
questions.answer: Sapwood is outer, light and functional; heartwood is inner, dark, hard, non-functional and more durable.

questions.q: Distinguish between racemose and cymose inflorescences (two points).
questions.answer: In racemose the main axis grows continuously and flowers are acropetal; in cymose the axis ends in a flower and flowers are basipetal.

questions.q: Differentiate between true fruit and false fruit.
questions.answer: A true fruit develops from the ovary alone (mango); a false fruit includes other floral parts such as the thalamus (apple).

questions.q: Mention two functions of the stem other than conduction.
questions.answer: Storage of food (potato) and vegetative propagation (rose, sugarcane).

questions.q: What are hydathodes? Write their function.
questions.answer: Water pores at the vein endings near leaf margins that exude liquid water with salts (guttation) in humid conditions.

questions.q: What is dendrochronology?
questions.answer: Determining the age of a tree by counting its annual growth rings.

questions.q: Name the types of stamens in (a) pea (b) mustard.
questions.answer: (a) Diadelphous. (b) Tetradynamous.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: With the help of a neat labelled diagram briefly explain the verticillaster type of inflorescence. Give one example.
questions.answer: A series of condensed dichasial cymes at each node with a cluster of sessile flowers in the axil of the opposite leaves, giving a whorl-like cluster all around the node; e.g. Ocimum (tulsi) and Salvia. (Draw an axis with nodes, each node showing a whorl of sessile flowers.)

questions.q: With the help of a neat labelled diagram briefly explain the hypanthodium inflorescence. Give one suitable example.
questions.answer: The receptacle is a fleshy, hollow cup with a small apical opening (ostiole); the inner wall bears male flowers near the opening and female flowers below; e.g. fig and peepal.

questions.q: Differentiate between the dicot stem and the monocot stem (any three points).
questions.answer: Dicot: hypodermis collenchymatous, vascular bundles in a ring and open, secondary growth present. Monocot: sclerenchymatous hypodermis, bundles scattered, closed with bundle sheath and a water cavity, no secondary growth.

questions.q: Differentiate between a stoma and a hydathode (three points).
questions.answer: Stomata are all over the leaf, lose water as vapour and open or close with light; hydathodes are at vein endings near margins, lose liquid water with salts and are always open.

questions.q: Describe phyllotaxy with examples.
questions.answer: Arrangement of leaves on a stem: alternate (one leaf per node; china rose, mango), opposite (pairs; decussate in tulsi and superposed in guava) and whorled (more than two per node; Nerium).

questions.q: Explain the modification of leaves with examples.
questions.answer: Tendrils (climb; pea), spines (protect and reduce transpiration; Opuntia), phyllode (flattened petiole; Australian acacia), pitcher (Nepenthes) and bladder (Utricularia) for trapping insects.

questions.q: Explain the types of placentation with one example each.
questions.answer: Marginal (pea), axile (china rose), parietal (mustard), basal (sunflower) and free central (Dianthus).

questions.q: Describe the types of vegetative modifications of subaerial stems.
questions.answer: Runner (grass), stolon (jasmine), offset (water hyacinth) and sucker (chrysanthemum): they lie on or partly in the soil, strike roots at nodes and propagate vegetatively.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Identify the modified plant part in the following: (1) Rhizome of ginger (2) Carrot (3) Spines of Opuntia (4) Thorns of Citrus (5) Phylloclade of Opuntia.
questions.answer: (1) Underground stem (storage and perennation). (2) Tap root (conical, storage). (3) Modified leaves (reduce transpiration and protect). (4) Modified axillary bud, a stem (protection). (5) Modified stem (photosynthesis and water storage).

questions.q: Describe the secondary growth in a dicot stem.
questions.answer: Fascicular and interfascicular cambium form a ring that adds secondary xylem inside and secondary phloem outside, with more xylem; cork cambium in the cortex forms cork outside and phelloderm inside; the periderm replaces the epidermis; lenticels aerate; bark is all the tissue outside the cork cambium; spring and autumn wood form annual rings.

questions.q: Describe the internal structure of a dicot stem.
questions.answer: Epidermis with hairs, hypodermis of collenchyma, parenchymatous cortex and endodermis (starch sheath), pericycle with sclerenchyma, vascular bundles in a ring (conjoint, collateral, open, endarch xylem), medullary rays and pith.

questions.q: Differentiate between the dicot leaf and the monocot leaf.
questions.answer: Dicot leaf is dorsiventral with stomata mostly on the lower surface, palisade and spongy tissue and no bulliform cells; monocot leaf is isobilateral with stomata on both surfaces, only spongy mesophyll and bulliform cells on the upper epidermis.

questions.q: Explain the various types of stem modifications with examples.
questions.answer: Underground: rhizome, corm, bulb, tuber; subaerial: runner, stolon, offset, sucker; aerial: tendril, thorn, phylloclade and cladode, with their functions.

questions.q: Describe the major kinds of fruits with examples.
questions.answer: Simple fruits (dry dehiscent such as pea legume, mustard siliqua; dry indehiscent such as wheat caryopsis; fleshy such as mango drupe, tomato berry, cucumber pepo, orange hesperidium, apple pome), aggregate (strawberry) and composite fruits (pineapple, fig).
